A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Context Reasoner and contain readable main text, figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A–E. Relocated and renumbered material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations of its SFT/PPO models on legal compliance, contextual understanding, and generalization benchmarks, including additional experiments in Appendix C.

after.justification: v2 retains these empirical results and adds CI/RL ablation and balanced-training experiments in Appendix C, Tables 15–16.

M1.justification: The proposed regulation/database construction, DeepSeek-R1 distillation, CI-structured cold start, and rule-reward PPO procedure remain unchanged. Removing CI or RL constitutes added ablation conditions rather than a revision of the proposed method.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the same legal domains, contextual-understanding questions, LegalBench, LawBench, TruthfulQA, MMLU, and Winogrande coverage. The new balanced-training experiment samples existing GDPR and EU AI Act cases without adding tasks or domains.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, OpenThinker-7B, and DeepSeek-R1 as comparators. Appendix C adds an explicitly evaluated RL-without-CI comparison variant against CI-containing SFT and the full CI+RL method in Table 15.

E3.justification: v2 adds CI/RL removal controls and a balanced-training experiment randomly sampling 300 cases per class for GDPR and EU AI Act. The main 8:2 split, evaluation metrics, and stated training settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix C gains focused tests separating CI and RL contributions and examining sensitivity to class-balanced training. Existing training-ingredient ablations, response-length analysis, PPO curves, and case studies are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. v2's discussion of result variance concerns class balancing and adds point estimates, not uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Existing benchmark scores and plotted results remain unchanged. New Table 15 reports average scores of 87.81 without RL, 86.36 without CI, and 88.29 with both. Table 16 adds balanced-training scores of 90.12/84.16 for GDPR/EU AI Act versus 92.19/84.33 using the whole training set. The headline gain also changes reference baseline, rather than model scores.

T1.justification: The CI definition, compliance condition, reward objective, and PPO mathematics are retained. Appendix D partly moves onto page 16; adding the theta subscript to the policy in explanatory prose is a notation clarification.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction revise the claimed legal-compliance gain from +17.64% to +8.58%. Unchanged Table 1 shows these correspond to 88.29 minus Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct's 70.65 and OpenThinker-7B's 79.71, respectively. The central CI/RL contribution and generalization claims remain.

C2.justification: v2 adds the tentative explanation that lower EU AI Act performance reflects the law's novelty, scarce real-world cases, and limited model exposure. The existing limitations concerning conflicts between regulations and remaining failure risks are unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 supplies a source-code repository link and explicitly states that distillation seed cases originate from the training split. Appendix C documents the new ablation conditions and 300-per-class sampling. Existing hardware, hyperparameters, generation settings, and prompts remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The introduction and references add Chen et al. (2025a,b), Cheng et al. (2025), Deng et al. (2025), Shi et al. (2025), and Yim et al. (2024), while removing Dong et al. (2024). Section 6's substantive positioning relative to prior CI and privacy work remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized edits to the abstract, introduction, and dataset description, adds analytical paragraphs in Appendix C, and introduces acknowledgments. The overall narrative and section organization are retained.

P2.justification: The MMLU and LegalBench tables exchange positions and numbers. Two new appendix tables are added, and existing prompt/example Tables 15–18 become Tables 17–20. Figures 1–5 retain their displays, with limited surrounding layout reflow.

improvement.justification: v2 adds useful component and class-balance checks, clarifies training-data provenance, and provides a source-code location. The revised headline gain better reflects the improvement over OpenThinker-7B in unchanged Table 1. These improve evidence and transparency incrementally, although the new ablation specifications remain brief and uncertainty estimates are still absent.
